item.content:encoded: The image that was used in this article is non-compliant with the SCP wiki's license (CC BY-SA 3.0) as it comes from Cornell University (as indicated here), with no indication it has been released under Creative Commons. Thus, the image has been removed.

item.content:encoded:
I like this one, but there is one minor issue. This bit,
"Unlike in eusocial arthropods, there is no queen. There are caste divisions in its population, however, including workers, soldiers, breeders, and nursery attendants."
The description is apt, but the arthropod bit kinda comes out of nowhere. I suggest reversing the two, and rewording them to fit. Contrasting with arthropods doesn't make sense without already having established that they have some similarities.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded: I don't think there was a problem with the pictures. The problem was with the way you had the pictures but didn't say they were naked mole rats. The impression it gave was, "Oh, this is obviously fake; those are just naked mole rats," which breaks suspension of disbelief. If you had said they were a different kind, though, it becomes, "Oh, okay, these are disgusting, horrible naked mole rats." Just acknowledge that they're a form of naked mole rat and move on. They're freaky little gits. Honestly, you'd make this article a lot creepier if you included a lot more actual naked mole rat biology. How about the queen? Or the fact that they don't feel pain?
